name: HDP's new initiatives for child education and nutrition

content.title: HDP's new initiatives for child education and nutrition
content.summary: The pilot programmes will be launched in several districts of Sindh

media.alt: HDP's new initiatives for child education and nutrition
HDP's new initiatives for child education and nutrition

content.text: As good health and nutrition are basic requirements for effective learning, the Aga Khan University's Human Development Programme has initiated two pilot programmes to mobilize communities and teachers to understand and respond to children's educational, nutritional and gender-related needs in Sindh.

The projects will be launched in Dadu, Hyderabad, Jacobabad, Kambar Shahdadkot, Kashmore, Khairpur, Larkana and Sukkur districts, and in five towns of Karachi including Bin Qasim, Gadap, Keamari, Lyari and Orangi.
The programmes are supported by grants from the U.S. Agency for International Development.

The Community Mobilization Program - part of the USAID-funded Sindh Basic Education Program running in partnership with the Sindh Education and Literacy Department, Government of Sindh - will link schools and health facilities to fight malnutrition.

Under the two-year project, HDP will train key stakeholders and roll out school-based education to improve hygiene and nutrition practices; work with communities to identify and address district-specific issues related to food availability and daily diet, and encourage a change in household dietary practices through community action. It is hoped that better awareness among teachers, parents and children can lead to improved nutrition.

The second programme on mainstreaming children with special educational needs and adolescent girls in government and private schools builds on HDP's previous work on children with disabilities and problems of girls' accessing education in Hyderabad and Sukkur districts. The 14-month programme introduces strategies to enhance the knowledge and skills of parents and teachers to manage children with physical or cognitive challenges, and increase the enrolment of girls aged 10-19.
The effort is part of the U.S. government's Let Girls Learn campaign to ensure girls get the education they deserve.

"AKU is not only an institution of academic excellence but also an agent for social development. The University prepares men and women to lead change in their societies, and they go where the need is greatest. These programmes have the potential to significantly change the lives of children at a disadvantage," said Dr Farhat Abbas, Dean, Medical College. "We are helping to identify how the poorest children who suffer from malnutrition and poor health, can attend and stay in school to complete their education in the hope of a better life."

"Education plays a vital role in improving children's health and nutrition," said the American Ambassador David Hale. "We believe a comprehensive strategy is required to address issues related to malnutrition, especially among affected children in Sindh," he added.

The ceremony was attended by U.S. Consul General Brian Heath, DG Health Sindh Dr Syed Hassan Murad Shah, USAID Provincial Director Craig Buck, Aga Khan University Hospital's CEO Hans Kedzierski, and HDP's Director Dr Ghazala Rafique.

Established in 2003, AKU's Human Development Programme endeavors to support human development through a multidisciplinary and research-based approach. Its initial focus is early childhood, with an integrated approach to education, health, nutrition and child development related to cognitive, social and emotional abilities. Its community-based interventions are directed to improving child nurture by providing appropriate information and skills development for mothers, their families and the wider community.
